text:
Maria Chen: kicked off an nsys trace for the vLLM <-> TensorRT wrapper on a single P4d instance. goal: find why tail latency spikes at ~1200 tokens for the new batching heuristic.

Maria Chen: command I used: `nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=run_vllm_trt  python -m tests.perf.trace_runner --scenario=multi-client`

Ajay Patel: nice. did you also collect perfetto traces for the host side? the scheduler overhead might be in user-space.

Maria Chen: yep, grabbed perfetto from the same run (recorded via `perfetto --txt -o perfetto.pb`). link: https://perfetto.local/trace/1766501234 (internal).

Zach Rivera: quick summary from nsys GUI: big chunks of time are in `wrapper::prepare_inputs` and `scheduler::enqueue_batch` before the TRT engine call. GPU kernels (int8 kernels) are fast, but there's long gaps between kernel launches. looks like CPU-side serialization and memcpy stalls. :thinking:

Irene K: can you paste the flamegraph snippet? curious about the relative sizes.

Maria Chen: pasted the hot span:
```
wrapper::run_batch  320ms
  wrapper::prepare_inputs  120ms
  scheduler::enqueue_batch  80ms
  trt_engine::invoke  60ms
    cudaMemcpyAsync  10ms
    infer_kernel_int8  40ms
  wait_for_cuda  60ms
```

Ajay Patel: that `wait_for_cuda` being 60ms is red flag. suggests CPU launches kernel then immediately blocks on a stream sync or host-side API. are we doing any synchronous `cudaStreamSynchronize` in the wrapper or in vLLM's scheduler?

Maria Chen: grep shows a `synchronize_if_debug()` call in the wrapper that we forgot to gate behind an env flag. looks like it triggers on `TRT_DEBUG=1` even though env is unset in some containers because of inherited shell profile.

Zach Rivera: oof. that would explain the gaps. but the `prepare_inputs` time is still high. what's in there?

Maria Chen: mostly host-side tensor packing + KV cache lookup on CPU. when KV cache miss rate is ~12% we build new KV blocks (memcpy + reorder) which takes ~90us per request, multiplied by tokens in batch it adds up.

Irene K: and the batching heuristic change increased batch coalescing frequency, so more requests are getting packed together and hitting the KV codepath more often?

Maria Chen: exactly. new heuristic coalesces smaller partials into bigger batches, which reduces kernel invocations but amplifies the CPU packing cost and cold KV misses. tradeoff is net win for throughput but tail latency suffers.

Ajay Patel: two quick experiments to run: 1) disable the unexpected sync and rerun nsys; 2) run a trace with KV cache pre-populated to measure only packing overhead.

Maria Chen: running experiment 1 now. will post results.

perf-bot: experiment 1 completed (run_vllm_trt_no_sync). summary: tail latency 25% lower, `wait_for_cuda` collapsed to ~5ms, `trt_engine::invoke` remains ~60ms. perfetto link: https://perfetto.local/trace/1766501301

Zach Rivera: great. that confirms the sync was the major culprit for gaps. next: look into vectorizing the packing and moving parts to CUDA kernels (or async pinned-buffer pipelining) to remove host-side stalls.

Irene K: also consider adaptive batching: if KV miss rate > X% then don't coalesce more than N requests. this keeps tail latency bounded.

Ajay Patel: +1. small follow-ups: add NVTX ranges around `prepare_inputs` and `kv_lookup`, rerun nsys to get clearer CUDA timeline markers; and add unit perf test that simulates high KV miss patterns.

Maria Chen: adding NVTX now. will schedule a quick pairing session tomorrow to prototype pinned buffer pipeline. thanks all :thumbsup:
